title: Riverlane and NVIDIA Demonstrate Accelerated QEC Decoder Calibration Using GPU Processing
key_facts: Riverlane (error-correction technology provider) and NVIDIA announced benchmarks for GPU-accelerated recalibration of quantum error-correction decoders
Decoder settings drift as physical qubits change over time, so they need frequent recalibration
Uses Riverlane's Local Clustering Decoder adapted for GPUs
On an H100 GPU, training epochs for surface codes drop from minutes to seconds
Logical error rates fell by several percent up to a factor of two versus uncalibrated settings
Method draws on prior-optimization work from Google Quantum AI
quote_evidence: By processing batch syndrome workloads in parallel across thousands of threads, the H100 GPU reduces surface-code training epochs from minutes to seconds.
optimizing the decoder priors against physical device drift yielded logical error rate (LER) reductions ranging from several percent up to a factor of two
why_it_matters_hint: Faster recalibration could make error correction easier to keep accurate as hardware drifts.
notes: Company-announced benchmarks; no outside review stated.
